recognize_zh: 兩顆被紅血球擠壓變形的小至中型淋巴樣細胞，染色質均勻、濃縮而平滑（無明顯核仁），胞質極少僅剩一圈淡藍色邊，符合正常B前驅細胞血原母細胞（hematogone），旁邊是一顆嗜中性球作為大小對照。
features: Two small to intermediate lymphoid cells deformed and molded by adjacent red cells
Very high N:C ratio with only a thin rim of pale blue agranular cytoplasm
Adjacent segmented neutrophil with pale granular cytoplasm for size comparison
describe_en: Smear shows two small to intermediate lymphoid cells with very high N:C ratios, scant pale blue agranular cytoplasm and homogeneous, smooth chromatin without visible nucleoli; the nuclei are molded by adjacent red cells. A segmented neutrophil is present nearby. The cells have the morphology of hematogones (normal B-cell precursors). Hematogones cannot be reliably separated from lymphoblasts by morphology alone; flow cytometry demonstrating a maturing antigen continuum (CD34/CD10/CD20/CD38 pattern) is required.

ddx.vs: Lymphoblasts may be morphologically identical, but flow cytometry shows an asynchronous, maturation-arrested immunophenotype rather than the normal continuous maturation pattern of hematogones.
Mature lymphocytes have coarser block-like chromatin and a more distinct rim of cytoplasm and lack immature markers such as CD34, CD10 and TdT.
CLL cells show clumped 'soccer ball' chromatin and smudge cells and are light-chain restricted CD5+/CD23+ mature B cells.
